### What engineering memory says:
The compress middleware currently supports gzip and deflate encodings. Based on the recent compression work by oobobench, adding Brotli support would involve updating the encoding selection logic to include 'br' in the supported compression types and ensuring the Accept-Encoding header negotiation properly handles Brotli requests. The middleware already has the foundation for encoding negotiation and content type filtering from the recent commits.

- `84cb4b2` (relevance 0.54): User (oobobench / bench@oobo.ai) committed 'fix(compress): respect Accept-Encoding when encoding option is set (#4951)' on 2026-05-28, updating the compression middleware to check the client's Accept-
- `93329ab` (relevance 0.43): User (oobobench / bench@oobo.ai) committed 'fix(compress): convert strong ETag to weak ETag when compressing (#4848)' on 2026-05-28, updating compression middleware to downgrade strong ETags to weak o

You have engineering memory tools available. If you need to understand how something was implemented before, call `mcp__oobo__recall` with a short query (e.g., 'compress middleware options pattern'). Use `mcp__oobo__search` to find code by intent. These tools are faster than grepping through files manually.

The compress middleware currently supports gzip and deflate encodings. Recent commits
have added contentTypeFilter, fixed Accept-Encoding handling, and added ETag
conversion from strong to weak when compressing.

Add Brotli (br) support to the compress middleware:
- Add "br" to the ENCODING_TYPES array in src/middleware/compress/index.ts
- Brotli should be preferred over gzip when the client supports it (higher priority
  in selectEncoding)
- The existing contentTypeFilter and threshold options must work with Brotli too
- The strong-to-weak ETag conversion must also apply when using Brotli
- Use the Web Compression Streams API (CompressionStream with "deflate-raw" is not
  Brotli — you may need to check if the runtime supports it and fall back gracefully)
- Add test cases that verify Brotli is selected when Accept-Encoding includes "br"
- Make sure existing gzip/deflate tests still pass

- oobo: Context beyond the diff - captures AI sessions, tokens, code attribution, semantic code search, and engineering memory via MCP. Use when the user asks about commit history with AI context, session history, code attribution, token usage, code search, or engineering memory.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	/**
2	 * @module
3	 * Compress Middleware for Hono.
4	 */
5	
6	import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
7	import { parseAccept } from '../../utils/accept'
8	import { COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX } from '../../utils/compress'
9	
10	export { COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX }
11	
12	const ENCODING_TYPES = ['gzip', 'deflate'] as const
13	type Encoding = (typeof ENCODING_TYPES)[number]
14	const cacheControlNoTransformRegExp = /(?:^|,)\s*?no-transform\s*?(?:,|$)/i
15	
16	type ContentTypeFilter = RegExp | ((contentType: string) => boolean)
17	
18	interface CompressionOptions {
19	  encoding?: Encoding
20	  threshold?: number
21	  contentTypeFilter?: ContentTypeFilter
22	}
23	
24	const selectEncoding = (
25	  header: string | undefined,
26	  candidates: readonly Encoding[]
27	): Encoding | undefined => {
28	  if (header === undefined) {
29	    return undefined
30	  }
31	  const accepts = parseAccept(header)
32	  const wildcardQ = accepts.find((a) => a.type === '*')?.q
33	  let best: { encoding: Encoding; q: number } | undefined
34	  for (const enc of candidates) {
35	    const explicit = accepts.find((a) => a.type.toLowerCase() === enc)
36	    const q = explicit ? explicit.q : (wildcardQ ?? 0)
37	    if (q === 1) {
38	      return enc
39	    } else if (q > 0 && (!best || q > best.q)) {
40	      best = { encoding: enc, q }
41	    }
42	  }
43	  return best?.encoding
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Compress Middleware for Hono.
48	 *
49	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/compress}
50	 *
51	 * @param {CompressionOptions} [options] - The options for the compress middleware.
52	 * @param {'gzip' | 'deflate'} [options.encoding] - The compression scheme to allow for response compression. Either 'gzip' or 'deflate'. If not defined, both are allowed and will be used based on the Accept-Encoding header. 'gzip' is prioritized if this option is not provided and the client provides both in the Accept-Encoding header.
53	 * @param {number} [options.threshold=1024] - The minimum size in bytes to compress. Defaults to 1024 bytes.
54	 * @param {RegExp | Function} [options.contentTypeFilter=COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX] - A RegExp or function to determine if the response Content-Type should be compressed.
55	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler} The middleware handler function.
56	 *
57	 * @example
58	 * ```ts
59	 * const app = new Hono()
60	 *
61	 * app.use(compress())
62	 *
63	 * // Compress only JSON responses
64	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: /^application\/json/ }))
65	 *
66	 * // Compress based on custom Content-Type logic
67	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: (type) => COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX.test(type) || type === "application/x-myformat" }))
68	 * ```
69	 */
70	export const compress = (options?: CompressionOptions): MiddlewareHandler => {
71	  const threshold = options?.threshold ?? 1024
72	  const candidates: readonly Encoding[] = options?.encoding ? [options.encoding] : ENCODING_TYPES
73	
74	  const contentTypeFilter = options?.contentTypeFilter ?? COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX
75	  const shouldCompress =
76	    typeof contentTypeFilter === 'function'
77	      ? (res: Response) => {
78	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
79	          return type && contentTypeFilter(type)
80	        }
81	      : (res: Response) => {
82	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
83	          return type && contentTypeFilter.test(type)
84	        }
85	
86	  return async function compress(ctx, next) {
87	    await next()
88	
89	    const contentLength = ctx.res.headers.get('Content-Length')
90	
91	    // Check if response should be compressed
92	    if (
93	      ctx.res.headers.has('Content-Encoding') || // already encoded
94	      ctx.res.headers.has('Transfer-Encoding') || // already encoded or chunked
95	      ctx.req.method === 'HEAD' || // HEAD request
96	      (contentLength && Number(contentLength) < threshold) || // content-length below threshold
97	      !shouldCompress(ctx.res) || // not compressible type
98	      !shouldTransform(ctx.res) // cache-control: no-transform
99	    ) {
100	      return
101	    }
102	
103	    const accepted = ctx.req.header('Accept-Encoding')
104	    const encoding = selectEncoding(accepted, candidates)
105	    if (!encoding || !ctx.res.body) {
106	      return
107	    }
108	
109	    // Compress the response
110	    const stream = new CompressionStream(encoding)
111	    ctx.res = new Response(ctx.res.body.pipeThrough(stream), ctx.res)
112	    ctx.res.headers.delete('Content-Length')
113	    ctx.res.headers.set('Content-Encoding', encoding)
114	
115	    // Convert strong ETag to weak ETag since compressed content is not byte-identical
116	    const etag = ctx.res.headers.get('ETag')
117	    if (etag && !etag.startsWith('W/')) {
118	      ctx.res.headers.set('ETag', `W/${etag}`)
119	    }
120	  }
121	}
122	
123	const shouldTransform = (res: Response) => {
124	  const cacheControl = res.headers.get('Cache-Control')
125	  // Don't compress for Cache-Control: no-transform
126	  // https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7234#section-5.2.2.4
127	  return !cacheControl || !cacheControlNoTransformRegExp.test(cacheControl)
128	}

21	  contentTypeFilter?: ContentTypeFilter
22	}
23	
24	type CompressionStreamCtor = new (format: string) => TransformStream<Uint8Array, Uint8Array>
25	
26	type BrotliFactory = () => TransformStream<Uint8Array, Uint8Array>
27	
28	let brotliFactoryPromise: Promise<BrotliFactory | null> | undefined
29	
30	// Resolve a Brotli stream factory once per process. Prefers the Web
31	// Compression Streams API; falls back to node:zlib so that Node.js runtimes
32	// without native CompressionStream('br') support (Node < 23) still work.
33	const getBrotliFactory = (): Promise<BrotliFactory | null> => {
34	  if (!brotliFactoryPromise) {
35	    brotliFactoryPromise = (async () => {
36	      try {
37	        new (CompressionStream as CompressionStreamCtor)('br')
38	        return () => new (CompressionStream as CompressionStreamCtor)('br')
39	      } catch {}
40	      try {
41	        const [{ createBrotliCompress }, { Duplex }] = await Promise.all([
42	          import('node:zlib'),
43	          import('node:stream'),
44	        ])
45	        return () =>
46	          Duplex.toWeb(createBrotliCompress()) as unknown as TransformStream<Uint8Array, Uint8Array>
47	      } catch {}
48	      return null
49	    })()
50	  }
51	  return brotliFactoryPromise
52	}
53	
54	const selectEncoding = <T extends Encoding>(
55	  header: string | undefined,
56	  candidates: readonly T[]
57	): T | undefined => {
58	  if (header === undefined) {
59	    return undefined
60	  }
61	  const accepts = parseAccept(header)
62	  const wildcardQ = accepts.find((a) => a.type === '*')?.q
63	  let best: { encoding: T; q: number } | undefined
64	  for (const enc of candidates) {
65	    const explicit = accepts.find((a) => a.type.toLowerCase() === enc)
66	    const q = explicit ? explicit.q : (wildcardQ ?? 0)
67	    if (q === 1) {
68	      return enc
69	    } else if (q > 0 && (!best || q > best.q)) {
70	      best = { encoding: enc, q }
71	    }
72	  }
73	  return best?.encoding
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * Compress Middleware for Hono.
78	 *
79	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/compress}
80	 *
81	 * @param {CompressionOptions} [options] - The options for the compress middleware.
82	 * @param {'br' | 'gzip' | 'deflate'} [options.encoding] - The compression scheme to allow for response compression. Either 'br', 'gzip', or 'deflate'. If not defined, all three are allowed and will be used based on the Accept-Encoding header. 'br' is prioritized when supported by both the runtime and the client; otherwise 'gzip' is preferred over 'deflate'.
83	 * @param {number} [options.threshold=1024] - The minimum size in bytes to compress. Defaults to 1024 bytes.
84	 * @param {RegExp | Function} [options.contentTypeFilter=COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX] - A RegExp or function to determine if the response Content-Type should be compressed.
85	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler} The middleware handler function.
86	 *
87	 * @example
88	 * ```ts
89	 * const app = new Hono()
90	 *
91	 * app.use(compress())
92	 *
93	 * // Compress only JSON responses
94	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: /^application\/json/ }))
95	 *
96	 * // Compress based on custom Content-Type logic
97	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: (type) => COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX.test(type) || type === "application/x-myformat" }))
98	 * ```
99	 */
100	export const compress = (options?: CompressionOptions): MiddlewareHandler => {
101	  const threshold = options?.threshold ?? 1024
102	  const candidates: readonly Encoding[] = options?.encoding ? [options.encoding] : ENCODING_TYPES
103	
104	  const contentTypeFilter = options?.contentTypeFilter ?? COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX
105	  const shouldCompress =
106	    typeof contentTypeFilter === 'function'
107	      ? (res: Response) => {
108	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
109	          return type && contentTypeFilter(type)
110	        }
111	      : (res: Response) => {
112	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
113	          return type && contentTypeFilter.test(type)
114	        }
115	
116	  return async function compress(ctx, next) {
117	    await next()
118	
119	    const contentLength = ctx.res.headers.get('Content-Length')
120	
121	    // Check if response should be compressed
122	    if (
123	      ctx.res.headers.has('Content-Encoding') || // already encoded
124	      ctx.res.headers.has('Transfer-Encoding') || // already encoded or chunked
125	      ctx.req.method === 'HEAD' || // HEAD request
126	      (contentLength && Number(contentLength) < threshold) || // content-length below threshold
127	      !shouldCompress(ctx.res) || // not compressible type
128	      !shouldTransform(ctx.res) // cache-control: no-transform
129	    ) {
130	      return
131	    }
132	
133	    const accepted = ctx.req.header('Accept-Encoding')
134	    let encoding = selectEncoding(accepted, candidates)
135	    if (!encoding || !ctx.res.body) {
136	      return
137	    }
138	
139	    let stream: TransformStream<Uint8Array, Uint8Array>
140	    if (encoding === 'br') {
141	      const brotliFactory = await getBrotliFactory()
142	      if (brotliFactory) {
143	        stream = brotliFactory()
144	      } else {
145	        // Brotli unsupported by the runtime; fall back to other accepted encodings.
146	        const fallback = selectEncoding(
147	          accepted,
148	          candidates.filter((c): c is Exclude<Encoding, 'br'> => c !== 'br')
149	        )
150	        if (!fallback) {
151	          return
152	        }
153	        encoding = fallback
154	        stream = new CompressionStream(fallback)
155	      }
156	    } else {
157	      stream = new CompressionStream(encoding)
158	    }
159	
160	    // Compress the response
161	    ctx.res = new Response(ctx.res.body.pipeThrough(stream), ctx.res)
162	    ctx.res.headers.delete('Content-Length')
163	    ctx.res.headers.set('Content-Encoding', encoding)
164	
165	    // Convert strong ETag to weak ETag since compressed content is not byte-identical
166	    const etag = ctx.res.headers.get('ETag')
167	    if (etag && !etag.startsWith('W/')) {
168	      ctx.res.headers.set('ETag', `W/${etag}`)
169	    }
170	  }
171	}
172	
173	const shouldTransform = (res: Response) => {
174	  const cacheControl = res.headers.get('Cache-Control')
175	  // Don't compress for Cache-Control: no-transform
176	  // https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7234#section-5.2.2.4
177	  return !cacheControl || !cacheControlNoTransformRegExp.test(cacheControl)
178	}
